args.title: checkout-api health check failures after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) after the latest deploy of v2.3.1, with error rate at ~18%.

Action taken: Rolled the service back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously healthy in production (deployment history: v2.2.9 healthy, v2.3.0 healthy, v2.3.1 unhealthy). Note that v2.3.1-rc also shows unhealthy, but it is a staging release and was not a rollback candidate.

The first rollback attempt partially failed (orchestrator error) and halted after us-east, leaving the fleet in a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). A retry completed the rollout successfully.

Current status: v2.3.0 confirmed running in all three regions, service reporting healthy with error rate down to ~0.2%.

Follow-up needed: Root-cause the v2.3.1 health check failures and error rate spike before any redeploy; v2.3.1 should not be re-released without investigation and change-manager approval.

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

**Diagnosis:** checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three production regions, unhealthy with an ~18% error rate. Release history showed v2.2.9 (healthy) → v2.3.0 (healthy) → v2.3.1 (unhealthy). v2.3.1-rc also shows unhealthy but is a staging release, so it wasn't a valid rollback target.

**Rollback to v2.3.0** (previously healthy in production — no change-manager approval required, since the policy only applies to versions never healthy in prod):
- First attempt failed with `partial_failure: orchestrator error`, halting after us-east and leaving a mixed fleet (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1).
- Retried; all three regions now on v2.3.0. Verified healthy, error rate down to ~0.2%.

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, for checkout-api, on-call paged. The first `create_incident` call timed out, so I retried with the same idempotency key — the listing confirms a single incident was created (no duplicate), and its summary records the rollback, the partial-failure/retry, and the current healthy state.

**Recommendation:** v2.3.1 needs root-causing before any re-release; it should not be redeployed without investigation (and change-manager approval, as it has never been healthy in production).
